title: The 4 Best Travel Neck Pillows for Long-Haul Flights
h1: The 4 Best Travel Neck Pillows for Long-Haul Flights
metaDescription: Our 4 picks for travel neck pillows for long-haul flights, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at travel neck pillows for long-haul flights using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: Cabeau Evolution S3 Travel Pillow
products.blurb: Key specs: Memory foam horseshoe with seat strap system, 360-degree head and neck support, Quick-dry, moisture-wicking cover.
strengths: Seat strap clips to the headrest wings and physically stops head drop even in deep sleep
Densest, most supportive memory foam of the group for 8+ hour flights
Quick-dry fabric holds up well on long flights where cabin humidity varies
Compresses down for the carry bag despite being the bulkiest pillow uninflated
limitations: Straps only work on economy seats with adjustable headrest wings
Bulkier packed size than the Trtl or an inflatable pillow
features: Memory foam horseshoe with seat strap system
Compresses to about a third of its size in the included carry bag

products.name: Trtl Pillow Travel Neck Pillow
products.blurb: Key specs: Scarf-style wrap with a hidden internal support plinth, Weighs about 4.5 ounces, Soft fleece exterior.
strengths: Packs almost flat, taking up a fraction of the space of a horseshoe pillow
Hidden internal plinth holds the head upright without a bulky foam collar
Doubles as a soft scarf against a cold cabin
Typically the lightest pillow in the category
limitations: One-size wrap fits a narrower range of neck sizes comfortably than adjustable models
No support for reclining or leaning the head back against a headrest
Less cushioning than a full memory foam horseshoe
features: Scarf-style wrap with a hidden internal support plinth

products.name: J-Pillow Travel Pillow
products.blurb: Key specs: J-shaped foam design supporting head, chin, and neck, Works in window, aisle, or middle seat orientation, Non-inflatable foam fill that holds its shape.
strengths: The chin support arm stops the mouth-open, head-bobbing sleep other shapes allow
Same shape works whether you lean toward the window or forward
Foam fill holds its shape night after night without needing to reinflate
Highest owner rating of the pillows in this list
limitations: Does not compress flat since it is solid foam, not inflatable
The asymmetric J-shape takes a flight or two to get used to
Bulkier to store in a bag pocket than a scarf-style pillow
features: J-shaped foam design supporting head, chin, and neck
Works in window, aisle, or middle seat orientation
Non-inflatable foam fill that holds its shape

products.name: MLVOC Inflatable Travel Pillow
products.blurb: Key specs: Inflatable U-shape with a micro-velvet cover, Includes eye mask, earplugs, and a drawstring bag, Deflates flat for packing.
strengths: Deflates down to pocket size, the most packable option once empty
Adjustable firmness by how much air you put in
Comes as a full kit with eye mask and earplugs included
Cheapest pillow in this list by a clear margin
limitations: Feels less plush than memory foam once you are a few hours in
Air valve can loosen slightly over a long flight, needing a quick top-up
Shorter long-term durability than the foam options here
features: Inflatable U-shape with a micro-velvet cover
Includes eye mask, earplugs, and a drawstring bag

howWeChose: Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. We don't claim our own testing.
We do not list prices or star ratings because they change. Check Amazon for current details.
